document.title: Rumsfeld snowflake to Douglas Feith, "Pakistan" ("Get the Paks to really fight")
document.authors: Office of the Secretary of Defense (Donald Rumsfeld)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Afghanistan 20/20: The 20-Year War in 20 Documents | National Security Archive
document.note: [Unclassified] Rumsfeld suggests getting a chunk of money to ease Musharraf's transition so Pakistan will fight the war on terror. It shows U.S. naivety about Pakistan and its intelligence service playing both sides; Musharraf received about $10 billion in U.S. aid over six years.

events.description: Rumsfeld sends a snowflake memo to Douglas Feith suggesting the US obtain a chunk of money to ease Musharraf's transition and get Pakistan to fight the war on terror.
Rumsfeld sends snowflake memo to Douglas Feith suggesting the US obtain a chunk of money to ease Musharraf's transition so Pakistan will fight the war on terror in its own country.

relationships.detail: Rumsfeld directs a memo to Feith asking him to respond on funding for Pakistan.
relationships.quote: Doug Feith ... Pakistan ... Please respond by

relationships.detail: Rumsfeld proposes a financial package to ease Musharraf's transition toward a position the US needs.
relationships.quote: get a chunk of money, so that we can ease Musharraf's transition

relationships.target: Office of the Secretary of Defense
relationships.detail: Rumsfeld authors the memo as Secretary of Defense; the document is attributed to the Office of the Secretary of Defense (OSD document footer).
Feith is tasked by Rumsfeld to respond to the memo, implying a subordinate relationship.
relationships.quote: don't you think we ought to get a chunk of money

relationships.detail: Musharraf is the leader whose government/country would be induced to fight the war on terror; implied head of Pakistan government.
relationships.quote: get the Paks to really fight the war on terror where it is, which is in their country

relationships.detail: The war on terror is described as being in the Paks' own country.
relationships.quote: fight the war on terror where it is, which is in their country

key_claims: Rumsfeld believed in June 2002 that the war on terror was located inside Pakistan.
He wanted Pakistan to fight terrorism more vigorously.
He proposed US financial assistance as a way to ease Musharraf's transition to the position the US wanted.
